Chapter Six: The Power of Kindness—To Self and Others
You know, kindness is a bit of a quiet superpower. It doesn’t come with bright lights or big announcements, but it can honestly shift the course of someone’s day—or even their entire life. Especially when things feel uncertain, kindness becomes this subtle way of standing up to fear and division.
Let me share a story. There’s a man who, after a tough week, found himself snapping at his partner over something that really didn’t matter. The air turned heavy, and both of them just retreated into silence. Later that night, he sat alone, feeling that familiar sting of regret. He remembered how, when he was a kid, his grandmother would always offer a cup of tea and a gentle word whenever tempers flared. She never tried to fix everything—she just made things feel softer, less sharp.
The next morning, this man decided to make breakfast for his partner. He left a simple note: “I’m sorry. I love you.” That small gesture made a huge difference. Suddenly, the conversation wasn’t about blame or who was right—it was about how hard things had been, and how much they cared for each other. By being kind to himself first—admitting his mistake—and then reaching out with kindness to his partner, he opened a door that had seemed closed.
Most of us don’t realize how powerful these little acts can be. Think about it—a smile to a stranger, a kind word to a coworker, just taking a deep breath and being patient when the line at the store feels endless. These tiny moments are what really hold us together, especially when the world feels a bit rough around the edges.
But here’s something a lot of people forget: kindness isn’t just something you give away. It’s something you need to show yourself, too. That same man learned to forgive his own slip-ups, to treat himself with the same gentleness he’d offer to someone he loves. Self-kindness isn’t about letting yourself off the hook—it’s about giving yourself a fighting chance. When you’re gentle with yourself, you’re actually able to show up better for everyone else.
So, when life feels uncertain, kindness is like a little light you can carry. It doesn’t magically fix everything, but it does make the darkness less overwhelming. Most people don’t realize just how much power they have to shape the mood around them—one small, genuine act at a time.
